        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

  "meta_commentary": "From-scratch project: only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py` exist at the working directory and BOTH must remain untouched at the project root \u2014 confirmed via T14. Use `pyproject.toml`'s `py-modules = [\\\"tool_schemas\\\"]` (NOT a copy/move) to make `from tool_schemas import TOOL_REGISTRY` work after `pip install -e .`; T12 adds an explicit smoke test as a regression guard. Stack is committed: Python 3.11+, FastAPI async, asyncpg + raw SQL (no ORM), pydantic-settings, single forward-only SQL migration via `psql`. Hard user constraint: NO pgvector, NO embedding columns, NO vector extension \u2014 dedup will be agentic-search in Plan 3. Migration must be re-run safe (`IF NOT EXISTS` + DO-block policy guards); teardown is local-dev only. RLS is deny-anon defense-in-depth; service role bypasses automatically \u2014 do not author per-user authenticated policies in this plan. `llm_spend_log` is operational and outside the spec's 11 tables; comment it as such in SQL. Heartbeat is in-process asyncio only \u2014 do NOT insert a `scheduled_jobs` row because 'heartbeat' is not in the `job_type` CHECK enum; real scheduling lands in Plan 5. Do NOT implement webhook handling, signature validation, LLM calls, OOB checker, weekly summary, decay, admin content, or feedback endpoints \u2014 those belong to Plans 2\u20136. Spend-cap helpers must EXIST and be tested but MUST NOT gate any call sites yet (no call sites exist in this plan). For SecretStr fields use `.get_secret_value()`; admin Basic Auth must use `secrets.compare_digest`. DB-backed tests should `pytest.skip` cleanly when `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset so the foundation can be validated without infra. Two open verifiability flags (live `/health` 200 and >24h heartbeat) are minor and covered by U2/U3 \u2014 they cannot be closed inside the executor session.",

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

  "meta_commentary": "From-scratch project: only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py` exist at the working directory and BOTH must remain untouched at the project root \u2014 confirmed via T14. Stack is committed: Python 3.11+, FastAPI async, asyncpg + raw SQL (no ORM), pydantic-settings, single forward-only SQL migration via `psql`. Hard user constraint: NO pgvector, NO embedding columns, NO vector extension \u2014 dedup will be agentic-search in Plan 3. Migration must be re-run safe (`IF NOT EXISTS` + DO-block policy guards); teardown is local-dev only. RLS is deny-anon defense-in-depth; service role bypasses automatically \u2014 do not author per-user authenticated policies in this plan. `llm_spend_log` is operational and outside the spec's 11 tables; comment it as such in SQL. Heartbeat is in-process asyncio only \u2014 do NOT insert a `scheduled_jobs` row because 'heartbeat' is not in the `job_type` CHECK enum; real scheduling lands in Plan 5. Do NOT implement webhook handling, signature validation, LLM calls, OOB checker, weekly summary, decay, admin content, or feedback endpoints \u2014 those belong to Plans 2\u20136. Spend-cap helpers must EXIST and be tested but MUST NOT gate any call sites yet (no call sites exist in this plan). For SecretStr fields use `.get_secret_value()`; admin Basic Auth must use `secrets.compare_digest`. DB-backed tests should `pytest.skip` cleanly when `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset so the foundation can be validated without infra. Two open verifiability flags (live `/health` 200 and >24h heartbeat) are minor and covered by U2/U3 \u2014 they cannot be closed inside the executor session.",

# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

}

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/docs/ops.md\n+# Operations\n+\n+This service exposes `GET /health` for uptime checks. The endpoint returns\n+`{\"status\":\"ok\",\"db\":\"ok\"}` only after the application can run `SELECT 1`\n+against the configured Postgres database.\n+\n+## Uptime Checks\n+\n+Use an external monitor such as UptimeRobot or Better Stack.\n+\n+1. Create an HTTP monitor pointed at `https://<your-railway-domain>/health`.\n+2. Use a 1 minute or 5 minute interval.\n+3. Treat any non-2xx response as down.\n+4. Configure alert routing outside this repo, for example email, Slack, or pager.\n+\n+For cron-style pings, configure the same monitor target:\n+\n+```sh\n+curl -fsS \"https://<your-railway-domain>/health\"\n+```\n+\n+Railway should also be configured with `healthcheckPath: \"/health\"` from\n+`railway.json`, so deploy health and external uptime checks use the same route.\n+\n+## Spend Counters\n+\n+Daily LLM spend counters live in Postgres table `llm_spend_log`.\n+\n+The primary key is `(provider, day)`. Supported provider names in application\n+helpers are:\n+\n+- `text`\n+- `vision`\n+- `transcription`\n+\n+Rows are updated by `record_llm_cost()` using an UPSERT that increments\n+`total_usd`. `is_under_cap()` reads today's row and compares it to the matching\n+settings cap.\n+\n+## Rotation Expectation\n+\n+Counters are keyed by calendar day, so no daily reset job is required for the\n+foundation plan. Keep historical rows for audit and cost review unless a later\n+retention policy says otherwise.\n+\n+Operational secret rotation is handled outside the app:\n+\n+- Rotate Supabase service-role keys and API keys in Railway environment\n+  variables.\n+- Redeploy or restart the Railway service after changing secrets.\n+- Verify `/health` after rotation.\n+- Confirm the next app log contains `heartbeat: alive at <utc_iso>`.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/README.md\n+# Mediator Bot Foundation\n+\n+Foundation scaffold for the mediator bot described in\n+[`mediator-bot-spec.md`](mediator-bot-spec.md). This repository currently\n+contains only the infrastructure layer: FastAPI app setup, env-backed settings,\n+Supabase/Postgres migrations, health/admin stubs, phone whitelist helper, and\n+spend-cap plumbing.\n+\n+`tool_schemas.py` lives at the repository root by design and must not be moved,\n+copied, renamed, or deleted. Packaging exposes it as the top-level\n+`tool_schemas` module.\n+\n+## Local Setup\n+\n+Use Python 3.11 or newer.\n+\n+```sh\n+python -m venv .venv\n+source .venv/bin/activate\n+pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n+cp .env.example .env\n+```\n+\n+Populate `.env` with real values before running the app against a real\n+database. Do not commit `.env`.\n+\n+## Environment Checklist\n+\n+Mirror these variables in local `.env` and Railway environment variables:\n+\n+- `ENV_NAME`\n+- `DATABASE_URL`\n+- `SUPABASE_URL`\n+- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`\n+- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`\n+- `OPENAI_API_KEY`\n+- `GROQ_API_KEY`\n+- `WHATSAPP_TOKEN`\n+- `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`\n+- `WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN`\n+- `WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`\n+- `ADMIN_PASSWORD`\n+- `PARTNER_PHONE_A`\n+- `PARTNER_PHONE_B`\n+- `TEXT_LLM_DAILY_CAP_USD`\n+- `VISION_DAILY_CAP_USD`\n+- `TRANSCRIPTION_DAILY_CAP_USD`\n+- `SENTRY_DSN`\n+- `LOG_DESTINATION`\n+\n+Optional values may be left blank when unused. Secret values must only live in\n+local `.env`, Railway variables, or the relevant provider control plane.\n+\n+## Apply Migrations\n+\n+Apply the forward migration with `psql`:\n+\n+```sh\n+psql \"$DATABASE_URL\" -f migrations/0001_init.sql\n+```\n+\n+The migration is intended as the first one-shot foundation migration. It is\n+written with `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, and\n+guarded policy `DO` blocks so accidental re-runs are safer, but it is still a\n+forward migration rather than a general migration manager.\n+\n+It creates 11 spec tables plus the operational `llm_spend_log` table. It enables\n+only `pgcrypto`; it must not create pgvector, embedding columns, or vector\n+storage.\n+\n+## Teardown\n+\n+For local development only:\n+\n+```sh\n+psql \"$DATABASE_URL\" -f migrations/teardown.sql\n+```\n+\n+Do not run `migrations/teardown.sql` against shared, staging, production, or\n+Supabase project databases.\n+\n+## Run Server\n+\n+```sh\n+uvicorn app.main:app --reload\n+```\n+\n+For Railway, the production command is:\n+\n+```sh\n+uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port \"$PORT\"\n+```\n+\n+## Run Tests\n+\n+```sh\n+pytest -q\n+```\n+\n+DB-backed tests skip when `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset. Set it to a scratch\n+database URL if you want spend and live health checks to run against Postgres.\n+\n+## Deploy To Railway\n+\n+1. Create a Railway service from this repository.\n+2. Keep the Nixpacks builder from `railway.json`.\n+3. Confirm the start command is\n+   `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`.\n+4. Add every variable from the environment checklist above.\n+5. Deploy and confirm Railway reports `/health` as healthy.\n+6. Configure an external uptime monitor for `/health`.\n+\n+See [`docs/ops.md`](docs/ops.md) for uptime monitoring, spend-counter location,\n+and rotation expectations.\n*** End Patch\n"
}

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

Does `/admin` use `secrets.compare_digest` against `settings.admin_[REDACTED]()` and return 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="admin"` when missing/wrong? Is the heartbeat asyncio task created in lifespan startup and cancelled on shutdown without writing to `scheduled_jobs`?
- SC12 (T12): Does `conftest.py` use `httpx.AsyncClient` + `ASGITransport` sharing app lifespan? Does `test_config_loads` monkeypatch all required envs and instantiate `Settings()`? Does `test_tool_schemas_importable` assert `from tool_schemas import TOOL_REGISTRY`?
- SC13 (T13): Does `README.md` walk through local setup, migrations, server run, tests, Railway deploy with env-var checklist, AND include the explicit note that `tool_schemas.py` must stay at root? Does `docs/ops.md` cover uptime cron + spend-cap location?
- SC14 (T14): Does `pytest -q` pass (with DB-dependent tests skipping cleanly when TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset)? Are `tool_schemas.py` and `mediator-bot-spec.md` byte-identical to their original state? Did the throwaway smoke script confirm 401/200 for `/admin` and was it then deleted?

Watch items to keep visible during execution:
- Hard constraint: NO pgvector extension, NO vector/embedding columns, NO embedding infra in any file. The migration must enable only `pgcrypto`.
- `tool_schemas.py` and `mediator-bot-spec.md` must remain at the project root with byte-identical contents — no move/copy/rename/edit/delete.
- Packaging must expose `tool_schemas` as a top-level py-module via `pyproject.toml` (`py-modules = ["tool_schemas"]`) so `from tool_schemas import TOOL_REGISTRY` works after `pip install -e .`.
- All 11 spec tables PLUS `llm_spend_log` must have RLS enabled with a deny-anon FOR ALL policy. Service role bypasses RLS automatically — note in SQL comments.
- Every CHECK constraint listed in the spec (direction, processing_state, charge, media_type when not null, status fields, severity, confidence, sentiment, health, target_type, feedback sentiment, source, job_type) must be present. `observations.significance` is nullable to support failed-scoring path but constrained 1..5 when set.
- All 6 partial indexes from spec §Index Strategy and GIN indexes on `observations.related_theme_ids`, `observations.supporting_message_ids`, `memories.related_theme_ids`, `watch_items.related_theme_ids` must be present.
- Heartbeat is an in-process asyncio loop only — do NOT insert into `scheduled_jobs` because 'heartbeat' is not in the spec's `job_type` CHECK enum. Real scheduling lands in Plan 5.
- `llm_spend_log` is operational and outside the spec's 11 tables — comment it as such in SQL. Do NOT gate any LLM call sites in this plan; helpers exist but are unused.
- DO NOT implement webhook/signature validation, LLM calls, OOB checker, observation/memory writes, or admin content. Those belong to Plans 2–6.
- Migration must be safely re-runnable: `IF NOT EXISTS` on tables/indexes and DO-block policy guards. Teardown is LOCAL DEV ONLY.
- `admin_password` and `supabase_service_role_key` are SecretStr — use `.get_secret_value()` and `secrets.compare_digest` for the admin Basic Auth comparison.
- Phone whitelist normalization is whitespace strip + optional leading `+` strip with exact-string compare; reject empty/None. No E.164 parser yet.
- Verifiability gaps from gate (open, minor): the live `/health` 200 against a real DB and the >24h heartbeat log require human/runtime observation — covered by U2 and U3 after deploy.
- Caps wired from settings (text $10, vision $2, transcription $1) — defaults match spec but must be overridable via env.

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

(os.fspath(ROOT) + \"\\n\").encode()}\n+    return _write_wheel(wheel_directory, files, project)\n*** End Patch\n"

Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

Watch items to keep visible during execution:
- Hard constraint: NO pgvector extension, NO vector/embedding columns, NO embedding infra in any file. The migration must enable only `pgcrypto`.
- `tool_schemas.py` and `mediator-bot-spec.md` must remain at the project root with byte-identical contents — no move/copy/rename/edit/delete.
- Packaging must expose `tool_schemas` as a top-level py-module via `pyproject.toml` (`py-modules = ["tool_schemas"]`) so `from tool_schemas import TOOL_REGISTRY` works after `pip install -e .`.
- All 11 spec tables PLUS `llm_spend_log` must have RLS enabled with a deny-anon FOR ALL policy. Service role bypasses RLS automatically — note in SQL comments.
- Every CHECK constraint listed in the spec (direction, processing_state, charge, media_type when not null, status fields, severity, confidence, sentiment, health, target_type, feedback sentiment, source, job_type) must be present. `observations.significance` is nullable to support failed-scoring path but constrained 1..5 when set.
- All 6 partial indexes from spec §Index Strategy and GIN indexes on `observations.related_theme_ids`, `observations.supporting_message_ids`, `memories.related_theme_ids`, `watch_items.related_theme_ids` must be present.
- Heartbeat is an in-process asyncio loop only — do NOT insert into `scheduled_jobs` because 'heartbeat' is not in the spec's `job_type` CHECK enum. Real scheduling lands in Plan 5.
- `llm_spend_log` is operational and outside the spec's 11 tables — comment it as such in SQL. Do NOT gate any LLM call sites in this plan; helpers exist but are unused.
- DO NOT implement webhook/signature validation, LLM calls, OOB checker, observation/memory writes, or admin content. Those belong to Plans 2–6.
- Migration must be safely re-runnable: `IF NOT EXISTS` on tables/indexes and DO-block policy guards. Teardown is LOCAL DEV ONLY.
- `admin_password` and `supabase_service_role_key` are SecretStr — use `.get_secret_value()` and `secrets.compare_digest` for the admin Basic Auth comparison.
- Phone whitelist normalization is whitespace strip + optional leading `+` strip with exact-string compare; reject empty/None. No E.164 parser yet.
- Verifiability gaps from gate (open, minor): the live `/health` 200 against a real DB and the >24h heartbeat log require human/runtime observation — covered by U2 and U3 after deploy.
- Caps wired from settings (text $10, vision $2, transcription $1) — defaults match spec but must be overridable via env.

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.

Watch items to keep visible during execution:
- Hard constraint: NO pgvector extension, NO vector/embedding columns, NO embedding infra in any file. The migration must enable only `pgcrypto`.
- `tool_schemas.py` and `mediator-bot-spec.md` must remain at the project root with byte-identical contents — no move/copy/rename/edit/delete.
- Packaging must expose `tool_schemas` as a top-level py-module via `pyproject.toml` (`py-modules = ["tool_schemas"]`) so `from tool_schemas import TOOL_REGISTRY` works after `pip install -e .`.
- All 11 spec tables PLUS `llm_spend_log` must have RLS enabled with a deny-anon FOR ALL policy. Service role bypasses RLS automatically — note in SQL comments.
- Every CHECK constraint listed in the spec (direction, processing_state, charge, media_type when not null, status fields, severity, confidence, sentiment, health, target_type, feedback sentiment, source, job_type) must be present. `observations.significance` is nullable to support failed-scoring path but constrained 1..5 when set.
- All 6 partial indexes from spec §Index Strategy and GIN indexes on `observations.related_theme_ids`, `observations.supporting_message_ids`, `memories.related_theme_ids`, `watch_items.related_theme_ids` must be present.
- Heartbeat is an in-process asyncio loop only — do NOT insert into `scheduled_jobs` because 'heartbeat' is not in the spec's `job_type` CHECK enum. Real scheduling lands in Plan 5.
- `llm_spend_log` is operational and outside the spec's 11 tables — comment it as such in SQL. Do NOT gate any LLM call sites in this plan; helpers exist but are unused.
- DO NOT implement webhook/signature validation, LLM calls, OOB checker, observation/memory writes, or admin content. Those belong to Plans 2–6.
- Migration must be safely re-runnable: `IF NOT EXISTS` on tables/indexes and DO-block policy guards. Teardown is LOCAL DEV ONLY.
- `admin_password` and `supabase_service_role_key` are SecretStr — use `.get_secret_value()` and `secrets.compare_digest` for the admin Basic Auth comparison.
- Phone whitelist normalization is whitespace strip + optional leading `+` strip with exact-string compare; reject empty/None. No E.164 parser yet.
- Verifiability gaps from gate (open, minor): the live `/health` 200 against a real DB and the >24h heartbeat log require human/runtime observation — covered by U2 and U3 after deploy.
- Caps wired from settings (text $10, vision $2, transcription $1) — defaults match spec but must be overridable via env.

        Idea:
# Plan 1 — Foundation: project scaffold + DB schema + infra

Authoritative spec: `mediator-bot-spec.md` in the project root. Read it in the prep phase. This plan only delivers the foundation that the rest of the system will be built on; do not implement application logic that belongs to later plans.

## Scope (in)
- Python 3.11+ FastAPI project skeleton, async, ready to deploy on Railway. Standard layout (`app/`, `app/main.py`, `app/config.py`, `app/db.py`, `app/models/`, `app/routers/`, `tests/`). Dependency management with `pyproject.toml` (or `requirements.txt` if simpler), `.env.example`, `Procfile`/`railway.json` as appropriate.
- Configuration loader pulling from env vars only (no secrets in code). Settings for: Supabase URL + service-role key, Anthropic API key, OpenAI API key, Groq API key, WhatsApp Cloud API token + phone-number-id + verify-token + app secret, admin password, sentry/log destination (optional), env name.
- All Supabase (Postgres) tables exactly as specified in the spec's "Data Model" section: `users`, `messages`, `memories`, `themes`, `watch_items`, `observations`, `out_of_bounds`, `scheduled_jobs`, `bot_turns`, `tool_calls`, `feedback`. Use `timestamptz` for all timestamps. Include all enum-like CHECK constraints on the columns the spec describes (direction, processing_state, charge, status fields, severity, confidence, etc.).
- All indexes from the spec's "Index Strategy" section, including the partial indexes and GIN indexes on array columns.
- Row Level Security policies as defense-in-depth (service role bypass; deny by default for anon).
- Migration tooling: a single forward-only SQL migration file that creates the schema; document how to apply it against Supabase. Include a teardown script for local dev.
- Daily LLM spend cap infrastructure (counters table or in-memory + persisted snapshot — pick the simplest): `llm_spend_log` keyed by (provider, day) with running cost, plus a small helper `record_llm_cost(provider, dollars)` and `is_under_cap(provider) -> bool`. Wire the starting caps from the spec ($5/day per partner text = $10 total, $2/day vision, $1/day transcription) as configurable. No actual gating of calls yet — just the plumbing and a unit test.
- Health endpoint `GET /health` that returns 200 when DB is reachable.
- Heartbeat: a daily "I'm alive" log line on a startup background task or scheduled job stub (job row, no execution yet — execution lands in Plan 5).
- Monitoring stub: README/ops doc showing how to wire an external uptime check + cron ping to `/health`.
- Phone-number whitelist config (two partner numbers in env), exposed as `is_allowed_phone(num) -> bool`. No webhook yet — that's Plan 2.
- Admin view stub: a single [REDACTED] `/admin` route that returns a placeholder HTML page. Real content lands in Plan 6.
- README with: how to run locally, how to run migrations, how to deploy to Railway, env var checklist.
- Pytest set up; one smoke test per major piece (config loads, DB session opens, health endpoint responds, spend-cap helpers work).

## Scope (out, deliberately)
- WhatsApp webhook handler and signature validation (Plan 2).
- Any LLM calls or tool implementations (Plan 3+).
- OOB guardrail or significance scoring logic (Plan 4).
- Scheduled job worker, weekly summary, decay (Plan 5).
- Admin view actual content, audit endpoints, feedback (Plan 6).

## Success criteria
- `must`: All 11 tables exist with correct columns, types, defaults, CHECK constraints, and indexes per spec.
- `must`: App starts locally, `/health` returns 200, all smoke tests pass.
- `must`: No secrets committed; `.env.example` lists every required key with a brief comment.
- `must`: RLS enabled on every table.
- `should`: Migration is idempotent or clearly one-shot with documented re-run path.
- `should`: README runnable by a new operator without prior context.
- `info`: Spend-cap helpers exist and are unit-tested but unused.

## Notes
- This is a from-scratch project. Working directory has only `mediator-bot-spec.md` and `tool_schemas.py`. Treat `tool_schemas.py` as a pre-existing reference for tool argument shapes — read it during prep but don't modify it in this plan.
- Use Pydantic v2 for settings + models.
- Prefer `asyncpg` + raw SQL or SQLModel/SQLAlchemy with async — pick one and be consistent.

User notes and answers:
- Hard constraint added by user post-init: NO vector store, NO embedding column, NO pgvector extension. Dedup of memories/observations is done via agentic search (the agent reads existing rows before writing) — see Plan 3. Do not add embedding infrastructure speculatively.
